newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch pay dispute with FedEx causes strike.
newsitem.headline: Dutch pay dispute with FedEx causes strike.

text.p: FNV, the largest Dutch union, is in dispute with Federal Express over pay, union spokeswoman Roelie Hidding said.
FNV members went on strike on Wednesday at several Dutch FedEx branches including Schiphol, Rijsbergen, Ridderkerk and Apeldoorn. There was no strike on Thursday.
FedEx spokesman for the Benelux, Peter Kluivers, said the union had accepted an invitation by the company to have a meeting but would not give the date and made no further comment.
FNV'S Hidding said the union was deciding on a day-to-day basis whether to take strike action and she estimated that 80 percent of FedEx staff had taken part in Wednesday's strike.
On Thursday, union members had decided not to strike because FedEx had brought in temporary workers. "Therefore they will have to pay the salaries of both," said Hidding.
Pay, especially for irregular working hours, is at the centre of the dispute, she said. Recently, a new salary system had been introduced without any consultation, she said.

"FedEx does not want to negotiate with the union and has said it will freeze salaries. The company also want to abolish the extra allowance for overtime work which is an important part of their salaries."
FedEx employs 150 people in the Netherlands. Until now, the union has kept quiet about these issues at the request of the employees to give FedEx time to reply, she said.
The FNV is calling for talks Thursday or Friday. However, FedEx has said it is unable to have a meeting until Monday November 18, Hidding claimed.
Belgian workers at FedEx are also supporting the strike although they are not taking action themselves, she stressed. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
